description: The main command. Can be prefixed with `-` (ignore non-zero exit), `+` (run as root regardless of User=), `!` (skip exec privileges), `:` (don't expand specifiers). Multiple ExecStart= for Type=oneshot.
Run before ExecStart. Failure aborts unit start. Multiple lines run sequentially; can prefix with `-` to tolerate failure.
Run after ExecStart confirmed started (Type-dependent: simple=immediately, exec=after execve, notify=after READY=1).
Run on stop request. If absent, systemd sends KillSignal.
Drop privileges to this user before ExecStart.
Allocate ephemeral UID/GID for this service. Implies sandboxing defaults.
CWD before ExecStart. ~ = home of User=.
chroot to this dir before exec.
Read env from file (one KEY=VAL per line). Prefix with `-` to tolerate missing file.
Inherit named env vars from systemd's environment.
Syslog facility for forwarded log lines.
Fresh user namespace (UID 0 inside, real user outside).
Make filesystem RO. strict = entire FS RO except /dev/proc/sys; full = /usr+/boot+/efi RO; true = /usr+/boot RO.
Set the prctl PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS bit. Required for unprivileged seccomp.
Errno returned for filtered syscalls (vs default = SIGSYS).
Restrict to listed personalities. native = current.
Forbid creating listed namespace types. e.g. RestrictNamespaces=~user net.
Forbid socket() with non-listed families. e.g. RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6 only.
Forbid creating files with setuid/setgid bits.
Forbid making memory both writable AND executable. Stops JIT-style attacks (and breaks legit JITs).
Cap-bounding-set. Whitelist (e.g. CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE) or blacklist (~CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE).
Ambient caps preserved across non-setuid execve. The way to give non-root services specific caps.
RLIMIT_CORE (max core file size). 0 disables core dumps.
What systemd does when service is OOM-killed.
Under ProtectSystem=strict, expose these as RW.
Auto-create /run/<PATH> at start, owned by service user, deleted at stop.
Soft dependency. Started together; failure tolerated.
Hard dependency. Failure of dep stops this unit.
Must already be active; doesn't start dep.
Stop this unit if dep stops (not just fails).
Stop+restart only when listed units stop+restart.
Activate listed units when this enters 'failed'. Used for alerting (e.g. notify-on-failure.service).
Activate listed units on success exit.
Whether systemctl isolate can switch to this target.
Auto-add Wants/After=basic.target, Conflicts/Before=shutdown.target. Disable for very-early-boot units.
What to do on job timeout.
Max starts per StartLimitIntervalSec before unit goes to 'failed' permanently.
Skip unit if path doesn't exist. Prefix `!` to invert.
Skip unless path is a dir.
Skip if RAM less/more than. e.g. ConditionMemory=>4G.
True only on first boot of the system (machine-id absence).
Like ConditionPathExists but FAILS unit on miss (vs silently skipping).
Forbid manual systemctl start (only via deps).
Service launch type. Affects when systemd considers unit 'active'.
Don't restart if exit status / killed by these signals.
Always restart on these (vs Restart= rule).
Exit codes/signals that count as success.
For Type=oneshot: stay 'active (exited)' after ExecStart completes.
For Type=forking: file containing main PID after fork.
For Type=forking with no PIDFile: try to identify main PID from cgroup.
For Type=dbus: name to wait for on bus.
Who can sd_notify. For Type=notify, must be at least 'main'.
How to kill processes on stop.
Also send SIGHUP after KillSignal (some daemons want this).
Place this unit in a specific slice.
Memory below which kernel won't reclaim. Hard protection.
Memory below which kernel prefers to keep. Best-effort.
Hard CPU quota. e.g. 50% = half a core, 200% = 2 cores.
Device-cgroup allowlist (DEVICE = path or major:minor; PERMS = rwm).
Delegate cgroup subtree to user (for nested resource control by service itself).
PSI memory pressure threshold for systemd-oomd kill.
TCP/UNIX-stream listening socket. Multiple lines = multiple sockets.
Open a special file (chardev) and pass FD.
yes = systemd accept()s + forks per-conn service@N. no = pass listen-FD to single service.
Max activations per interval before socket disabled.
Time after systemd start to fire.
Time after timer activated to fire.
Time after target unit last activated to fire next. The 'every N hours' periodic style.
Time after target unit last deactivated.
Allowed slack for batching. Default 1min lets timers be coalesced.
Random delay derived from machine-id (consistent across boots, varies between hosts).
For OnCalendar=: if missed (system off), run on next boot.
Wake system from suspend to fire.
Unit to activate. Default = same name with .service suffix.
Source to mount. Same as fstab field 1.
Mount point. MUST match unit name (mountpoint encoded → unit name).
Filesystem type. ext4, xfs, nfs, etc.
umount -l (detach immediately, clean up when last user closes).
Disable RO fallback if RW mount fails.
Create file (and write content). e.g. f /run/foo 0644 root root - 'hello'. Lowercase = idempotent.
Like d but clears contents on --clean.
Create btrfs subvolume (or directory if not btrfs).
Remove file or empty dir on --remove.
Create the watched dir if missing.
Forward Secure Sealing (cryptographic chain). Requires sealing key.
Max messages per service per window.
Min free space to leave on filesystem.
Max single file size before rotation.
Where cores go: nowhere | files in /var/lib/systemd/coredump | inline in journal.
Max RSS for a process to dump core (skip larger).
Max size of external core file.
Runtime dir: /run for system, /run/user/UID for user.
State dir: /var/lib for system, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME for user.
Catalog message ID (lookup in catalog with -x).
